name: Aggressive Natural Killer (NK)-Cell Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of a clonal proliferation of NK cells in peripheral blood with leukemic features
Detection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in neoplastic NK cells by in situ hybridization
NK-cell immunophenotype: CD2+, surface CD3-, cytoplasmic CD3ε+, CD56+, CD16 variable
Rapidly progressive clinical course with systemic symptoms and hepatosplenomegaly
Bone marrow infiltration by atypical NK cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clonal NK-cell proliferation in peripheral blood with EBV positivity and characteristic immunophenotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, morphological, immunophenotypic, and virological data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) positivity in NK cells

searchTerms: enlarged liver and spleen with symptoms
big liver and spleen causing illness
low red blood cells with pale skin

occasional.symptomName: Hepatic dysfunction with elevated liver enzymes

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement

rare.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to pulmonary infiltration
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to lung infiltration

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to leukemic infiltration

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing atypical large granular lymphocytes with azurophilic granules
Positive EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization
imaging: Hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT scan
genetic: Clonal rearrangement of NK-cell receptors not typically detected
Frequent chromosomal abnormalities including deletions in 6q and 11q
other: Immunophenotyping by flow cytometry showing CD2+, surface CD3-, cytoplasmic CD3ε+, CD56+, variable CD16 expression

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly extranodal involvement with nasal or midline facial lesions
Similar EBV association but different clinical presentation
Predominantly T-cell phenotype rather than NK-cell

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cytopenias with systemic symptoms
Evidence of EBV-positive NK-cell proliferation in peripheral blood
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Suzuki R. Aggressive NK-cell leukemia: a distinct clinical entity among mature T- and NK-cell neoplasms. Int J Hematol. 2014;99(3):247-256.
Kimura H. Epstein-Barr virus-associated T/natural killer-cell lymphoproliferative disorders. Front Pediatr. 2019;7:117.
